question.content: Why do twentieth century advances not seem sustainable ?

options.label: A
options.content: They do not meet the human needs

options.label: B
options.content: Due to the increased cost of agricultural production

options.label: C
options.content: Because they are outdated for the current times

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: According to the passage, 'Since twentieth century advances, given increasing costs, do not seem sustainable...'

question.content: What pushes farmers into places unsuited for agriculture ?

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: The passage states that 'Global population growth... has pushed farmers and herders into areas unsuited to intensive agriculture'.

question.content: Which one of the following is NOT true, according to the passage, for ecological degradation ?

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: World War II is mentioned as a time landmark ('since World War II'), whereas the other factors are cited as causes or aspects of ecological degradation.

question.content: What is the conclusion of the author in the passage about the prospects of agriculture in the world ?

options.label: A
options.content: The author is both hopeful and sceptical of the prospects of agriculture

options.label: B
options.content: The author is very hopeful of the prospects of agriculture

options.label: C
options.content: The author is sceptical of the prospects of agriculture

options.label: D
options.content: The author is neither hopeful nor sceptical of the prospects of agriculture

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: The author mentions remaining hopeful about humankind's agricultural prospects while simultaneously stating we can scarcely look forward optimistically, showing a stance that is both hopeful and sceptical.

question.content: Which one of the following words means 'incursion' ?

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: 'Incursion' means an invasion or a sudden attack or entry into a place.

question.content:
Convert from direct into indirect speech.
Ayushi said to the group, “We have had enough of suffering today. It is time to march forward.”

options.label: A
options.content: Ayushi told the group that they had had enough of suffering that day and it was time to march forward

options.label: B
options.content: Ayushi asked the group that they had had enough of suffering this day and it was time to march forward

options.label: C
options.content: Ayushi told the group that they had enough of suffering and that it is time to march forward

options.label: D
options.content: Ayushi told the group that we had had enough of suffering this day and it was time to march forward

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: In indirect speech, 'said to' changes to 'told', 'We' changes to 'they', 'have had' changes to 'had had', 'today' changes to 'that day', and 'is' changes to 'was'.

question.content:
Convert from direct into indirect speech.
“Alas! We lost the match by one point,” said the Captain

options.label: A
options.content: The Captain regretted that they had lost the match by one point

options.label: B
options.content: The Captain regretted that they lost the match by one point

options.label: C
options.content: The Captain exclaimed that they had lost the match by one point

options.label: D
options.content: The Captain told the team that they had lost the match by one point

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: 'Alas!' expresses regret/sorrow. The simple past tense 'lost' changes to past perfect 'had lost' in indirect speech.

question.content:
Convert from direct into indirect speech.
“Where were you last week ?” Alok asked Sheela

options.label: A
options.content: Alok told Sheela where she had been the week before

options.label: B
options.content: Alok asked Sheela where she had been the week before

options.label: C
options.content: Alok asked Sheela where she was the week before

options.label: D
options.content: Alok asked Sheela where she had been the last week

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: In reporting interrogative sentences starting with 'Where', simple past 'were' changes to past perfect 'had been', and 'last week' changes to 'the week before'.

question.content: Directions : Following items have sentences in active voice with four options. One of the options converts the active voice into passive voice correctly. Select the most appropriate option and mark your answer on the Answer Sheet. The king who the people loved built the castle five centuries ago

options.label: A
options.content: The castle was built five centuries ago by the king who was loved by the people

options.label: B
options.content: The castle was built five centuries ago by the king who loved the people

options.label: C
options.content: The castle built five centuries ago by the king loved by the people

options.label: D
options.content: The castle was built five centuries ago by the people who were loved by the king

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: The main verb 'built' changes to passive 'was built', and the relative clause 'who the people loved' (active) changes to 'who was loved by the people' (passive).

question.content: The company has recruited four hundred engineers who will have to complete an internship for three weeks

options.label: A
options.content: Four hundred engineers have been recruited by the company and an internship of three weeks will have to be completed by them

options.label: B
options.content: Four hundred engineers have been recruited by the company and they will have to complete an internship of three weeks

options.label: C
options.content: The company has been recruited by four hundred engineers and an internship of three week will have to be completed by them

options.label: D
options.content: Four hundred engineers have been recruited by the company. Internship of three weeks will have had to be completed by them

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: Both active verbs 'has recruited' -> 'have been recruited' and 'will have to complete' -> 'will have to be completed' are properly converted into the passive voice.

question.content: Directions : In the following items, a pair of words is provided. You are required to select the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both the words and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly. Seldom and Often

options.label: A
options.content: Seldom means hardly ever and often means time and again

options.label: B
options.content: Seldom means time and again and often means hardly ever

options.label: C
options.content: Seldom means never and often means not at all

options.label: D
options.content: Seldom means frequently and often means time and again

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: 'Seldom' means rarely or hardly ever, while 'often' means frequently or time and again.

question.content: Overview and Review

options.label: A
options.content: Overview means assessment and review means general idea

options.label: B
options.content: Overview means general idea and review means assessment

options.label: C
options.content: Overview means general analysis and review means go through

options.label: D
options.content: Overview means summary and review means evaluation

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: An 'overview' provides a general idea or summary of something, whereas a 'review' involves a formal assessment or examination.

question.content: Overcome and Succeed

options.label: A
options.content: Overcome means triumph over and succeed means to achieve something

options.label: B
options.content: Overcome means achieve something and succeed means to triumph over

options.label: C
options.content: Overcome means to be successful and succeed means to achieve something

options.label: D
options.content: Overcome means winning and succeed means to rise above

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: 'Overcome' means to succeed in dealing with a problem or to triumph over it, while 'succeed' means to achieve something.

question.content: Embed and Imbue

options.label: A
options.content: Embed means instil and imbue means implant

options.label: B
options.content: Embed means implant and imbue means instil

options.label: C
options.content: Embed means accept and imbue means detest

options.label: D
options.content: Embed means include and imbue means accept

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: 'Embed' means to fix firmly and deeply in a surrounding mass (implant), and 'imbue' means to inspire or permeate with a feeling or quality (instil).

question.content: Emancipate and Empower

options.label: A
options.content: Emancipate means authorize and empower means liberate

options.label: B
options.content: Emancipate means liberate and empower means authorise

options.label: C
options.content: Emancipate means liberal and empower means authorisation

options.label: D
options.content: Emancipate means freedom and empower means encounter

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: 'Emancipate' means to set free from restrictions (liberate), and 'empower' means to give authority or power (authorise).

question.content: Directions : In the following items a sentence or a phrase is given with a word that is underlined, followed by four words or group of words. Select the option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly. The Professor has been able to \underline{instil} confidence in her students

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: 'Instil' means to gradually firm or establish an idea or attitude in a person's mind, which is closest in meaning to 'inculcate'.

question.content: The members of the group expressed their \underline{allegiance} to their leader

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: 'Allegiance' refers to loyalty or commitment to a superior, group, or cause.

question.content: The \underline{inscrutability} surrounding the incident remains unresolved until the end of the movie

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: 'Inscrutability' means the quality of being difficult to understand or interpret, which means 'mystery'.

question.content: The \underline{dodgy} behaviour of the leader led to her fall

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: 'Dodgy' means questionable, dubious, or suspicious.

question.content: People have been advised not to venture into sea as the weather is likely to be \underline{inclement}

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: 'Inclement' weather means unpleasantly cold, wet, or stormy weather, which is synonymous with 'squally'.

question.content:
Directions : In this section each item consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences in each have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. You are required to find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark your response accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

S1. Sufism is an English word coined in the Nineteenth Century
S6. It may also have been $suffa$, the platform outside a place of Islamic worship
P. Historians have understood this term in several ways
Q. According to some scholars, it is derived from $suf$, meaning wool
R. Others derive it from $safa$, meaning purity
S. The word used for Sufism in Islamic texts is $tasawwuf$

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: Sentence S introduces the Islamic term $tasawwuf$. P states that historians understand this term in several ways. Q and R follow with specific derivations ($suf$, $safa$), leading to S6 ($suffa$). Thus, the logical order is S P Q R.

question.content:
S1. Al-Biruni was born in 973, in Khwarizm in present-day Uzbekistan
S6. He arrived in Ghazni as a hostage, but gradually developed a liking for the city
P. In 1017, when Sultan Mahmud invaded Khwarizm, he took several scholars back to his capital, Ghazni : Al-Biruni was one among them
Q. He was well versed in several languages; Syriac, Arabic, Persian, Hebrew, and Sanskrit
R. Khwarizm was an important centre of learning, and Al-Biruni received the best education available at the time
S. However he did not know Greek, although he was familiar with the works of Plato and other Greek philosophers

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: S1 establishes Al-Biruni's birthplace. R elaborates on Khwarizm as a center of learning. Q and S discuss his language skills and knowledge of Greek philosophy. P explains the move to Ghazni, which directly connects to S6. Thus, the sequence is R Q S P.

question.content:
S1. Vijayanagara or 'city of victory' was the name of both a city and an empire
S6. They remembered it as Hampi, a name derived from that of the local mother goddess, Pampadevi
P. In its heyday it stretched from the river Krishna in the north to the extreme south of the Indian peninsula
Q. Although it fell into ruin in the seventeenth-eighteenth centuries, it continued to live in the memories of the people who inhabited the Krishna-Tungabhadra doab
R. In 1565 the city was sacked and subsequently deserted
S. The Empire was founded in the fourteenth century

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: S1 defines the empire/city. S gives its founding period. P describes its peak extent. R details its fall in 1565. Q mentions it remaining in memory, leading smoothly into S6. Thus, the correct sequence is S P R Q.

question.content:
S1. Liberalisation and globalisation freed India's economy from the low GDP trap that had impeded India's progress
S6. Today India has transformed into one of the largest economies of the world
P. India's 3 pc rate of growth and a set of emergent circumstances led to a balance of payment crisis in the early 1990s
Q. Ease of business was ensured, and the requirement for import licences, and production quotas, were removed
R. Apart from these measures India also took a loan from the IMF to tide over the crisis, but after 1993, India has not taken another loan from the IMF
S. In a landmark budget in 1991, responding to the emergent crisis, India delicenced many industries and liberalised its economic policies

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: P describes the background crisis of the early 1990s. S follows with the 1991 budget response. Q details specific economic measures. R adds that India took an IMF loan as part of these measures. S6 concludes with India's transformation today. Thus, the order is P S Q R.

question.content:
S1. In many countries, there are millions of people who are underprivileged and deprived
S6. In the past forced labour was imposed by landlords, money-lenders, and other wealthy persons
P. Both of these are prohibited under the Constitution of India
Q. One such form of exploitation in our country has been $begar$ or forced labour without payment
R. The marginalised are often subjected to exploitation by their fellow human beings
S. Another closely related form of exploitation is buying and selling of human beings and using them as slaves

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: R connects general deprivation (S1) to exploitation by fellow human beings. Q introduces one form of exploitation ($begar$). S introduces another related form. P refers back to "Both of these" forms of exploitation being prohibited. Thus, R Q S P is the proper sequence.

question.content:
Directions : Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker and mark your response accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

I can't be bothered to tell him what I think; _________ he would not listen to me.

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: "In any case" is used to introduce a reason that makes the previous statement true regardless of circumstances.

question.content: _________, if the referee points his fingers, this indicates that someone has done something wrong.

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: "Briefly" is used as a discourse marker to introduce a concise summary statement.

question.content: ___________, have you been to the local library yet ?

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: 'Incidentally' is used to introduce a new topic or question into a conversation.

question.content: ___________, women are healthier and are living longer than ever before : indeed on an average, they can expect to live five years longer than men.

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: 'To a large extent' means to a great degree or mostly, which fits the broad general statement.

question.content: The difference is that I have been fortunate to find a career that I love and, ___________, I am getting paid reasonably for it.

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: 'What is more' means in addition or furthermore, connecting two positive statements.

question.content: ___________, the Government of India has followed the policy of trying to improve relations with its neighbours.

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: 'In general' is an adverbial phrase used to describe an overall policy or broad trend.

question.content: ___________, this issue is likely to be discussed when the Council meets next.

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: 'As per reports' introduces news or reported information about upcoming events.

question.content: ___________, you needed to consult a physician to have a clear idea of what the disease is about.

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: 'In that case' is used to refer to a given condition or scenario.

question.content: ___________, in the year-ago period the current account deficit stood at $1.3$ billion or $0.2\%$ of the GDP.

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: 'Notably' is used to introduce a noteworthy or significant fact/statistic.

question.content: ___________, the records have been completely undermined by shoddy book-keeping.

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: 'As such' means in that capacity or as a result of the specified situation.

question.content: Infelicity :

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: Infelicity refers to an inappropriate or unsuitable remark, action, or expression.

question.content: Corollary :

options.label: B
options.content: Something that looks real but does not really exist

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: A corollary is a proposition that follows from one already proved, or a direct and natural consequence.

question.content: Quandary :

options.label: A
options.content: Situation in which you are confused about what to do

options.label: B
options.content: Situation in which two people or group argue

options.label: C
options.content: Situation in which no progress can be made

options.label: D
options.content: Situation in which a relationship becomes friendlier

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: A quandary is a state of perplexity or uncertainty over what to do in a difficult situation.

question.content: Presumption :

options.label: D
options.content: Opinion formed before having all the facts

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: Presumption means an idea that is taken to be true on the basis of probability before full facts are known.

question.content: Smug :

options.label: A
options.content: Too confident about one's own achievements

options.label: B
options.content: Too eager to help or obey someone important

options.label: D
options.content: Too eager to bottle up conflicts

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: Smug means having or showing an excessive pride in oneself or one's achievements.

question.content: of children they also contain deeply embedded (P) / whereas traditional fairy tales (Q) / moral lessons that are relevant even for adults (R) / were designed for the entertainment (S)

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: The logically coherent sentence order is Q-S-P-R: 'whereas traditional fairy tales (Q) were designed for the entertainment (S) of children they also contain deeply embedded (P) moral lessons that are relevant even for adults (R)'.

question.content:
P: of school education is an ineluctable truth
Q: that sporting activities are an integral part
R: meaningfully towards the overall growth of a student
S: that underscores the learning process and contributes

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: The correct sequence is Q P S R: 'that sporting activities are an integral part of school education is an ineluctable truth that underscores the learning process and contributes meaningfully towards the overall growth of a student'.

question.content:
P: and contentment on account of a life lived
Q: the beneficial outcome of
R: well without retribution or rebuke
S: a virtuous life is peace of mind

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: The correct sequence is Q S P R: 'the beneficial outcome of a virtuous life is peace of mind and contentment on account of a life lived well without retribution or rebuke'.

question.content:
P: more representative than the latter
Q: from a non-parliamentary system
R: in as much as the former is
S: it is widely believed that the parliamentary system differs

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: The correct sequence is S Q R P: 'it is widely believed that the parliamentary system differs from a non-parliamentary system in as much as the former is more representative than the latter'.

question.content:
P: crushes the spirit behind the service
Q: it stunts the person offering the same and
R: exhibition or for fear of public opinion
S: when service is done for

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: The correct sequence is S R Q P: 'when service is done for exhibition or for fear of public opinion it stunts the person offering the same and crushes the spirit behind the service'.

question.content: It does not look like he is going ________ in his studies than what was predicted by his school principal.

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: 'Any further' is used in negative constructions to express any additional degree or extent, fitting for academic progress.

question.content: ________ all the confusion the thief made a quiet getaway.

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: 'Amidst' is appropriate when referring to being in the middle of a condition or continuous state like 'all the confusion'.

question.content: The intricate operation on the patient required the expertise of a/an ________ surgeon.

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: 'Specialist surgeon' correctly specifies a doctor who concentrates on a specific branch of medicine.

question.content: There are ________ thirty students inside the classroom at any time.

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: 'Fewer than' is used with countable plural nouns such as 'students'.

question.content: There are many ________ vehicles on the highway due to a sudden landslide.

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: 'Stranded' describes vehicles that are stuck and unable to leave due to an obstacle like a landslide.

question.content: The focal length of a concave lens is $0.5\text{ m}$. The power of the lens is

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: For a concave lens, the focal length is negative, so $f = -0.5\text{ m}$. The power of the lens is $P = \frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{-0.5\text{ m}} = -2.0\text{ D}$.

question.content: The rule to determine the direction of a force experienced by a straight current carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field which is perpendicular to it is

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: Fleming's left-hand rule gives the direction of magnetic force acting on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.

question.content: One parsec in astronomical units (A.U.) is about

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: $1\text{ parsec} \approx 3.086 \times 10^{16}\text{ m}$ and $1\text{ A.U.} \approx 1.496 \times 10^{11}\text{ m}$. Therefore, $1\text{ parsec} \approx \frac{3.086 \times 10^{16}}{1.496 \times 10^{11}} \approx 2.06 \times 10^5\text{ A.U.} \approx 2 \times 10^5\text{ A.U.}$

question.content: Which one of the following statements for second law of motion is NOT correct?

options.label: A
options.content: The net force on a body is proportional to that body's acceleration

options.label: B
options.content: The net force on a body is in the same direction as the acceleration

options.label: C
options.content: The time rate of change of momentum is equal to force

options.label: D
options.content: The net force on a body is proportional to that body's momentum

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: Net force is proportional to the rate of change of momentum, not momentum itself.

question.content: The temperature of a body increases from $310\text{ K}$ to $340\text{ K}$. The temperature increase in degree Celsius is

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: The change in temperature on the Kelvin scale is equal to the change in temperature on the Celsius scale: $\Delta T = 340 - 310 = 30\text{ K} = 30^\circ\text{C}$.

question.content: Which one of the following statements for the work done by gravity on a body is NOT correct?

options.label: A
options.content: Work done is independent of the path followed by the body

options.label: B
options.content: Work done depends only on the vertical distance separating the initial and the final position of the body

options.label: C
options.content: Work done depends on the path followed by the body

options.label: D
options.content: Work done is zero if the body is displaced horizontally to the force of gravity

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: Gravity is a conservative force, which means work done by gravity is independent of the path followed.

question.content: Which one among the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.content: Pressure has magnitude as well as direction

options.label: B
options.content: As we go deeper in a liquid, the pressure decreases

options.label: C
options.content: Action and reaction forces act on the same object

options.label: D
options.content: Pascal and $\text{N/m}^2$ represent the same unit

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: $1\text{ Pascal (Pa)} = 1\text{ N/m}^2$. Therefore, both represent the same unit of pressure.

question.content: Which one of the following wave-length radiations may correspond to an X-ray?

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: X-rays typically have wavelengths ranging from about $0.01\text{ nm}$ to $10\text{ nm}$. Thus, $1\text{ nm}$ corresponds to X-rays.

question.content: In a Telescope, compared to the eyepiece lens the objective lens has

options.label: A
options.content: larger focal length and larger aperture

options.label: B
options.content: larger focal length and smaller aperture

options.label: C
options.content: smaller focal length and larger aperture

options.label: D
options.content: smaller focal length and smaller aperture

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: In an astronomical telescope, the objective lens has a larger focal length to increase magnification and a larger aperture to collect more light from distant objects.

question.content: The energy, $E$, of a photon can be expressed as $E = h f$ where $f$ is the frequency and $h$ is Planck's constant. The dimensions of $h$ are the same as that of

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: Dimensions of Planck's constant $h$ are $[\text{M}^1 \text{L}^2 \text{T}^{-1}]$, which are identical to the dimensions of angular momentum.

question.content: The work done by the force acting on an object is zero if the displacement of the object

options.label: A
options.content: is in the opposite direction of the direction of force

options.label: B
options.content: is in the same direction of the direction of force

options.label: C
options.content: is in perpendicular direction of the direction of force

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: Work done is given by $W = F s \cos\theta$. When force and displacement are perpendicular ($\theta = 90^\circ$), $\cos 90^\circ = 0$, so $W = 0$.

question.content: The magnetic field inside a current carrying very long solenoid is

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: Inside a very long current-carrying solenoid, the magnetic field lines are straight, parallel, and uniformly spaced, indicating a uniform magnetic field.

question.content: Which one of the following instruments can be used to measure $-250^	ext{C}$ temperature ?

options.label: A
options.content: By using a mercury based thermometer

options.label: B
options.content: By using an alcohol based thermometer

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: Mercury freezes at $-39^	ext{C}$ and alcohol freezes around $-114^	ext{C}$. To measure extremely low temperatures like $-250^	ext{C}$, thermocouple-based thermometers are used.

question.content: The quantity of heat needed to change unit mass of a substance from liquid to vapour without changing the temperature, is called

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: The amount of heat required to convert a unit mass of a liquid into vapour without a change in temperature is known as specific latent heat of vaporization.

question.content: The temperature at which "vapour pressure of the liquid in an open vessel becomes equal to the atmospheric pressure" is called

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: The boiling point of a liquid is the temperature at which its vapour pressure equals the external atmospheric pressure.

question.content: Which one of the following statements about surface tension is correct ?

options.label: C
options.content: It will remain same with increase or decrease of temperature

options.label: D
options.content: It will always decrease with increase or decrease of temperature

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: Surface tension of a liquid decreases with an increase in temperature due to the weakening of cohesive forces between molecules.

question.content: A body sinks in water when

options.label: A
options.content: density of water is greater than density of body

options.label: B
options.content: density of water is less than density of body

options.label: C
options.content: density of water is equal to density of body

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: A body sinks in water if its density is greater than the density of water (i.e., density of water is less than density of body), causing the weight of the body to exceed the buoyant force.

question.content: Why a fielder in the ground gradually pulls his hands backward while catching a fast moving cricket ball ?

options.label: A
options.content: To reduce the acceleration of the ball

options.label: B
options.content: To increase the acceleration of the ball

options.label: C
options.content: To increase the velocity of the ball

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: By pulling hands backward, the fielder increases the time taken to bring the ball to rest, thereby decreasing the rate of change of momentum (retardation/acceleration), which reduces the force exerted on his hands.

question.content: Bottom of a tank containing water appears to be raised. It is due to

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: Refraction occurs when light travels from a denser medium (water) to a rarer medium (air), causing rays to bend away from the normal, making the bottom appear raised.

question.content: SONAR stands for

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: SONAR is an acronym for Sound Navigation and Ranging.

question.content: Which one of the following radiations has longer wavelength ?

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: In the electromagnetic spectrum, microwaves have a longer wavelength compared to infra-red, ultraviolet, and X-rays.

question.content: For a material under static conditions, which one among the following statements is correct ?

options.label: B
options.content: A perfect conductor can be charged

options.label: C
options.content: Both perfect conductor and insulator can be charged

options.label: D
options.content: Both perfect conductor and insulator cannot be charged

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: An insulator can easily retain static electric charges on its surface when charged, as electrons cannot freely move through it.

question.content: A person can see nearby objects clearly but cannot see distant object distinctly, the person is suffering with

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: Myopia (nearsightedness) is a condition where nearby objects are seen clearly, but distant objects appear blurred.

question.content: The energy is always conserved for a system which is

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: The law of conservation of energy states that total energy remains constant in an isolated system, where no matter or energy is exchanged with the surroundings.

question.content: Suppose, a ball of mass M is thrown upwards from a point A and it reaches up to the highest point B and returns back to point A, which one among the following is correct ?

options.label: A
options.content: Kinetic Energy at A = Potential Energy at B

options.label: B
options.content: Kinetic Energy at A = Potential Energy at A

options.label: C
options.content: Kinetic Energy at B = Potential Energy at B

options.label: D
options.content: Kinetic Energy at B = Kinetic Energy at A

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: According to the conservation of mechanical energy, all the initial kinetic energy at point A is completely converted into potential energy at the highest point B.

question.content: Who among the following presided over the first session of All India Kisan Sabha in Lucknow in April 1936 ?

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati presided over the first session of the All India Kisan Sabha held at Lucknow in April 1936, with N. G. Ranga as General Secretary.

question.content: Who among the following founded the 'Self-Respect Movement' ?

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: The Self-Respect Movement was founded in 1925 by E. V. Ramaswami Naicker (Periyar) in Tamil Nadu.

question.content: Chola inscriptions mention several categories of lands. Which one of the following was meant for the maintenance of school ?

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: In Chola land classifications, Shalabhoga was land gifted for the maintenance of a school.

question.content:

question.content: In the Harappan Civilization, traces of canals have been found at

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: Traces of canal irrigation systems of the Harappan civilization have been discovered at Shortughai in Afghanistan.

question.content:
Arrange the following foreign travellers to India in chronological order, beginning with the earliest :
1. Peter Mundy

answer.explanation: The chronological order is Ibn Battuta (14th century), Afanasii Nikitin (15th century), Antonio Monserrate (16th century), and Peter Mundy (17th century), which gives 4 - 3 - 2 - 1.

question.content: With which of the following was the Bretton Woods System NOT associated

options.label: B
options.content: Economic recovery after the Second World War

options.label: C
options.content: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development

options.label: D
options.content: Establishment of a monetary system based on floating exchange rate

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: The Bretton Woods System established a fixed exchange rate system tied to gold/USD, not a floating exchange rate system.

question.content: Senguttuvan is the name of

options.label: D
options.content: the capital city of the Cheras

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: Cheran Senguttuvan was a famous Chera ruler of the Sangam period.

question.content: The Ramacharita, an example of dvyasrya-kavya, telling two stories simultaneously, was written by

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: The Ramacharita was written by Sandhyakar Nandi (Sandhyakara). It is a Sanskrit epic poem written in dvyasraya kavya style, simultaneously narrating the story of the Ramayana and the Pala King Ramapala.

question.content: Which of the following Acts established the Board of Control to guide and control the work of the Court of Directors and the Government of India ?

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: Pitt's India Act of 1784 established a Board of Control to supervise and direct all operations of the civil and military government and revenues of the British possessions in India.

question.content: Who among the following Sikh Gurus laid the foundation of the Khalsa Panth ?

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru, established the Khalsa Panth on the day of Baisakhi in 1699.

question.content: Which one among the following plans is also known as Mahalanobis Plan ?

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: The Second Five Year Plan (1956-1961) was based on the Mahalanobis model, which emphasized rapid industrialization and heavy basic industries.

question.content: Which of the following were the years of Annual Plans ?

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: The period between 1966 and 1969 is known as the 'Plan Holiday', during which three annual plans were implemented due to the failure of the Third Five Year Plan.

question.content:
Consider the following statements about BRICS Summits :

Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?

question.content:
Placing the earliest first, arrange the following international events in the chronological order :

1. Introduction of www (World Wide Web)
2. Advent of Inter-Continental Ballistic Missiles
3. Launch of first communication satellite

Select the answer using the code given below :

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: The advent of ICBMs occurred in 1957 (Soviet R-7 Semyorka). The first active communication satellite (SCORE/Telstar) was launched in 1958/1962. The World Wide Web was introduced in 1989. Thus, the chronological order is 2 - 3 - 1.

question.content:
Which of the following rights under the Constitution of India is/are Fundamental Right(s) ?

1. Right to work
2. Right to privacy
3. Right to free and compulsory education in the age bracket of six to eighteen years

Select the answer using the code given below :

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: 1. Right to work is a Directive Principle of State Policy (Article 41), not a Fundamental Right. 2. Right to privacy is a Fundamental Right under Article 21. 3. Right to education under Article 21A applies to children aged six to fourteen years, not six to eighteen years. Therefore, only statement 2 is correct.

question.content:

Incorrect: UN flag features a single pair of olive branches surrounding the world map. 3. Correct: ASEAN flag has blue, red, white, and yellow colours. Hence, only 1 statement is correct.

question.content: Which one of the following committees is NOT associated with decentralization of Panchayati Raj institutions in India ?

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: The Abhijit Sen Committee (2002) was set up to formulate a Long-Term Grain Policy, whereas the Balwant Rai Mehta, Ashok Mehta, and L. M. Singhvi committees were associated with Panchayati Raj institutions.

question.content: The reaction that occurs on passing carbon dioxide gas through lime water is

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: Lime water is calcium hydroxide solution $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$. Passing carbon dioxide through it forms calcium carbonate $\text{CaCO}_3$ (insoluble white precipitate) and water.

question.content: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?

options.label: A
options.content: Water of crystallization is the fixed number of water molecules present in one formula unit of a salt

options.label: B
options.content: The molecular formula of Plaster of Paris is $\text{CaSO}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$

options.label: C
options.content: Washing soda is used for removing the permanent hardness of water

options.label: D
options.content: The atmosphere of Venus is made up of thick white and yellow clouds of sulphuric acid

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: The chemical formula of Plaster of Paris is $\text{CaSO}_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}\text{H}_2\text{O}$ (calcium sulphate hemihydrate). $\text{CaSO}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is the formula for Gypsum.

question.content: Which one of the following type of medicines is used for treating indigestion?

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: Antacids neutralize excess stomach acid and are used to treat indigestion.

question.content: Which one of the following is NOT present in cement?

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: Portland cement contains dicalcium silicate ($2\text{CaO} \cdot \text{SiO}_2$), tricalcium silicate ($3\text{CaO} \cdot \text{SiO}_2$), and tricalcium aluminate ($3\text{CaO} \cdot \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$), but does not contain tetracalcium silicate ($4\text{CaO} \cdot \text{SiO}_2$).

question.content: Which one of the following is NOT a chemical change?

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: Melting of ice is a physical change because it involves a state change (solid to liquid) without changing the chemical composition of water.

question.content: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?

options.label: A
options.content: The interconversion of states of matter is a physical change

options.label: B
options.content: During burning of a candle, both chemical and physical changes take place

options.label: C
options.content: During a physical change, the chemical composition of molecules changes

options.label: D
options.content: Rusting of iron is a chemical change

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: During a physical change, the chemical composition of molecules remains unchanged.

question.content: Which one of the following is NOT a heterogeneous mixture?

options.label: B
options.content: Mixture of sugar and salt crystals

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: Sulphur dissolves completely in carbon disulfide to form a homogeneous solution.

question.content:
Match List I with List II and select the answer using the code given below the Lists:

List I (Element):
A. Phosphorus
B. Nitrogen
C. Neon
D. Sulphur

List II (Atomicity):
1. 2
2. 1
3. 8
4. 4

Code:
   A   B   C   D

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: Phosphorus exists as $P_4$ (atomicity 4, A-4); Nitrogen exists as $N_2$ (atomicity 2, B-1); Neon is monoatomic $Ne$ (atomicity 1, C-2); Sulphur exists as $S_8$ (atomicity 8, D-3). Hence, the correct code is 4 1 2 3.

question.content:
In the following redox reaction, which compound is acting as a reducing agent?
$\text{N}_2\text{H}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{N}_2 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: In $\text{N}_2\text{H}_4$, nitrogen has an oxidation state of -2 which increases to 0 in $\text{N}_2$. Since $\text{N}_2\text{H}_4$ undergoes oxidation, it acts as the reducing agent.

question.content: Which one of the following is considered to be the purest source of water?

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: Rain water is formed by natural evaporation and condensation, making it the purest form of natural water before reaching the ground.

question.content: Which one of the following salts is responsible for temporary hardness of water?

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: Temporary hardness of water is caused by the presence of dissolved bicarbonates of calcium and magnesium.

question.content:
Match List I with List II and select the answer using the code given below the Lists :

List I (Reaction)
A. $\text{CaO (s)} + \text{H}_2\text{O (l)} \rightarrow \text{Ca(OH)}_2\text{ (aq)}$
B. $\text{CaCO}_3\text{ (s)} \rightarrow \text{CaO (s)} + \text{CO}_2\text{ (g)}$
C. $\text{Pb (s)} + \text{CuCl}_2\text{ (aq)} \rightarrow \text{PbCl}_2\text{ (aq)} + \text{Cu (s)}$
D. $\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4\text{ (aq)} + \text{BaCl}_2\text{ (aq)} \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4\text{ (s)} + 2\text{NaCl (aq)}$

List II (Type)
1. Single displacement
2. Double displacement
3. Combination
4. Decomposition

Code :
     A   B   C   D

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: A is a Combination reaction ($A \rightarrow 3$), B is a Decomposition reaction ($B \rightarrow 4$), C is a Single displacement reaction ($C \rightarrow 1$), and D is a Double displacement reaction ($D \rightarrow 2$). Thus, the correct sequence is 3-4-1-2.

question.content: Which one of the following is an endothermic reaction ?

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: Thermal decomposition of lead nitrate requiring absorption of heat is an endothermic reaction.

question.content: Which one of the following is known as 'water gas' ?

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: Water gas is a synthesis gas containing a mixture of carbon monoxide ($\text{CO}$) and hydrogen ($\text{H}_2$).

question.content: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct ?

options.label: A
options.content: Diamond is hard due to extended covalent bonding in it

options.label: B
options.content: Fullerene is composed of five and six membered rings

options.label: C
options.content: Diamond is a good conductor of electricity

options.label: D
options.content: Graphite is used as a lubricant

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: Diamond lacks free electrons because all four valence electrons of carbon are used in single covalent bonds; hence, diamond is a bad conductor of electricity.

question.content:
Arrange the following zones in ascending order in terms of their latitudinal extent on the Earth surface :

1. Equatorial zone
2. Midlatitude zone
3. Subarctic zone
4. Tropical zone

answer.explanation: The latitudinal ranges are approximately: Equatorial zone (10° extent), Subarctic zone (10°-15° extent), Tropical zone (20° extent), and Midlatitude zone (30° extent). Thus, the ascending order is 1 - 3 - 4 - 2.

question.content:
Consider the following statements with reference to Feldspar mineral :

2. It has light cream to salmon pink colour
3. Magnesium is a common element in all types of feldspar

Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?

answer.explanation: Silicon and oxygen are common in all types of feldspar, not magnesium. Statements 1 and 2 are correct according to standard physical geology.

Consider the following pairs with reference to sedimentary rocks and the process of their formation :

answer.explanation: All three pairs are correctly matched according to standard classification of sedimentary rocks.

question.content:
Which of the following statements is/are correct ?

1. Oceanic trenches are very significant in the study of plate movements
2. Oceanic trenches are associated with active volcanoes and strong earthquakes

Select the answer using the code given below :

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: Oceanic trenches mark subduction zones where plates converge, leading to active volcanism and deep-focus earthquakes.

question.content:
Which of the following statements with reference to shadow zones in an event of an earthquake is/are correct ?

1. Zone between 105° and 145° from epicentre was identified as the shadow zone for both P-waves and S-waves
2. The shadow zone of P-waves is much larger than that of the S-waves

Select the answer using the code given below :

answer.label: A
answer.explanation: The shadow zone of S-waves is much larger than that of P-waves (extending beyond 105° everywhere), making statement 2 incorrect.

question.content: Which one among the following volcanic island chains is NOT associated with mid-oceanic ridge ?

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: Hawaiian Islands are formed by intraplate hotspot volcanism in the Pacific Plate and are NOT associated with a mid-oceanic ridge. Azores, Ascension, and Tristan da Cunha are associated with the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.

question.content: Consider the following statements with reference to sea waves : 1. The height of waves is determined by wind speed, wind duration, and fetch 2. The energy of a wave is proportional to the square of its height 3. Waves retain most of their energy as they travel across the deep ocean Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: All three statements are correct. Wave height is determined by wind speed, wind duration, and fetch. The energy of a wave is proportional to the square of its height ($E \propto H^2$). Waves retain most of their energy as they travel across the deep ocean as swells.

question.content: Which of the following statements with reference to soil forming processes is/are correct ? 1. Translocation, enrichment, removal and transformation are different classes of soil forming processes 2. In translocation, fine particles are transported downward by eluviation and accumulate in lower horizons by illuviation Select the answer using the code given below :

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: Both statements are correct. Soil-forming processes include additions (enrichment), losses (removal), translocations, and transformations. In translocation, eluviation transports particles downward and illuviation accumulates them in lower horizons.

question.content: Consider the following statements with reference to structure of the Earth's atmosphere : 1. Thickness of the troposphere is greatest at the equator 2. The air temperature of the tropopause is highest above the poles 3. The temperature in troposphere decreases at the rate of $1^\circ\text{F}$ for every $165\text{ m}$ of height Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The troposphere is thickest at the equator (~18 km), making the tropopause temperature above the equator lower (around $-80^\circ\text{C}$) than above the poles (around $-45^\circ\text{C}$). Statement 3 is incorrect because the temperature decreases at the rate of $1^\circ\text{C}$ (normal lapse rate) for every $165\text{ m}$, not $1^\circ\text{F}$.

question.content: Which of the following are the factors that cause variation in the amount of insolation on the Earth ? 1. Rotation of the earth on its axis 2. Length of the day 3. Distribution of land and water on the earth Select the answer using the code given below :

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: The primary factors causing variation in insolation received at the Earth's surface include the rotation of the Earth on its axis, the angle of inclination of the sun's rays, the length of the day, atmospheric transparency, and the distribution/configuration of land and water.

question.content: Consider the following conditions favourable for the formation and intensification of Tropical Storms : 1. Presence of the Coriolis force 2. Upper divergence above the sea level system 3. High variations in the vertical wind speed Which of the conditions given above is/are correct ?

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: Favourable conditions for tropical cyclone formation include the presence of Coriolis force and upper-level divergence above a low-pressure sea-level system. Statement 3 is incorrect because low (small) variation in vertical wind speed is required; high wind shear prevents cyclone formation.

question.content: Which of the following factors influence the ocean currents ? 1. Coriolis force 2. Gravity 3. Heating by solar energy 4. Wind Select the answer using the code given below :

answer.label: D
answer.explanation: Primary forces that initiate and influence ocean currents are heating by solar energy (causing thermal expansion), wind, gravity, and the Coriolis force.

question.content: Which of the following is/are warm ocean current(s) ? 1. Alaska Current 2. Agulhas Current 3. Falkland Current 4. West Australian Current Select the answer using the code given below :

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: Alaska Current and Agulhas Current are warm ocean currents. Falkland Current and West Australian Current are cold ocean currents.

question.content: State of Assam shares borders with how many other countries and Indian states respectively ?

answer.label: B

question.content: Which one of the following is the northernmost river basin of the Deccan Plateau ?

question.content:

question.content: Which one among the following is NOT a beneficiary state from the Vindhyachal Power Plant of the NTPC ?

question.content: The amount of air breathed in and out during a normal respiration by human lungs is referred to as

answer.label: B
answer.explanation: Tidal volume is the volume of air inspired or expired during normal respiration.

question.content: Which one among the following statements about arteries and veins in humans is NOT correct ?

options.content: Arteries carry blood away from heart while veins bring blood towards the heart

options.label: B
options.content: Pulmonary arteries always carry oxygenated blood while Pulmonary veins always carry deoxygenated blood

options.label: C

question.content: Identify the functions that are controlled by the hind brain of human being

question.content: What is the nickname of the National Men's Hockey Team of Australia ?

question.content:

question.content:
Which of the following were added in India as Ramsar Site in the year 2025 ?
1. Sakkarakottai Bird Sanctuary
2. Udhwa Lake
3. Rudrasagar Lake
4. Bakhira Wildlife Sanctuary
Select the answer using the code given below :

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: Sakkarakottai Bird Sanctuary (Tamil Nadu) and Udhwa Lake Bird Sanctuary (Jharkhand) were designated as Ramsar sites in 2024/2025.

question.content:
Consider the following statements about Cricket player Virat Kohli :
1. He is the only captain to have scored seven double centuries in Test Cricket
2. He is the only Indian cricketer with most centuries as a captain
3. He is the first Indian captain to achieve twin centuries on captaincy debut
4. He holds the record for the most double centuries by an Indian in Test Cricket
Which of the statements given above are correct ?

answer.label: C
answer.explanation: Statements 1, 3, and 4 are correct. Virat Kohli scored 7 double centuries in Test cricket, all while serving as captain, which is the highest by any captain and by an Indian player in Test history. He also scored centuries in both innings (115 & 141) on his Test captaincy debut at Adelaide in 2014.
